summary: After upgrading to v1.30.x, clusters experience continuous ringpop membership churn due to a pagination bug fix that now reads stale pod IPs from Cassandra. The excessive churn (~4000 events/30s) combined with extended join timeouts causes inter-service EOF errors, preventing workflow execution.
userImpact: Clusters become unable to execute workflows after upgrade due to continuous service connection failures and membership churn, requiring manual intervention or downtime to resolve.
rootCause: Stale pod IPs accumulate in cluster_membership table with 48h TTL; v1.30.x pagination fix now reads all entries while v1.29.x's pagination bug masked them. Additionally, ringpop join timeout (30s) is insufficient for large bootstrap lists across multiple Kubernetes node pools.
proposedFix: Reduce upsertMembershipRecordExpiryDefault from 48h to ~5m; expose ringpop config parameters (maxJoinDuration, ParallelismFactor) as configurable; optionally trim bootstrap list before passing to ringpop
workaround: Configure maxJoinDuration: 60s in static config (global: membership: maxJoinDuration: 60s); or scale cluster to 0 and back up to clear stale membership records
keyQuote: the cluster exhibits permanent ringpop membership churn (~4000 ring change events per 30 seconds). The membership ring sees 17 members when only 4 pods are running — the extra 13 are zombie IPs from previous pod restarts
